title: Invertible modules on projective bundles over arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_S$-module of constant rank $r\geq2$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let $p:P=\mathbf P_S(E)\to S$ be the bundle of one-dimensional quotients with tautological invertible module $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. For every invertible $\mathcal O_P$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], there are a unique locally constant function $d:|S|\to\mathbf Z$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module $N$, unique up to isomorphism, such that $L\simeq\mathcal O_P(d)\otimes p^*N$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Here $\mathcal O_P(d)$ is defined on $p^{-1}(d^{-1}(m))$ as $\mathcal O_P(1)^{\otimes m}$, using the dual line for negative $m$, and glued across these disjoint open subsets. Equivalently every point of $S$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which $L|_{P_U}\simeq\mathcal O_{P_U}(m)$ for an integer $m$. Tensor products add the functions $d$ and tensor the modules $N$. Under any base change $h:T\to S$ this description pulls back to $(d\circ|h|,h^*N)$. In particular, over a field every invertible module on $\mathbf P^{r-1}$ is a unique integer twist of $\mathcal O(1)$.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7, printed p.75: Picard decomposition for locally Noetherian connected bases. Arbitrary-base formulation is the agent extension by finite-presentation descent, using literature/stacks-project/limits.tex, Tag 0B8W (lemma-descend-invertible-modules), and the field normalization in literature/stacks-project/divisors.tex, Tag 0BXJ (lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD), with projective dimension at least one.

proof.text: Finite local freeness of E gives local freeness, hence quasi-coherence. For any normalized tautological quotient D apply the local-normal-form theorem to obtain local twists for every invertible L and its unique field normal form. Apply local-twist descent to those local forms to get the unique global degree and coefficient class. Both sides of local_iff hold for every invertible L, so the two implications follow from existence and the local theorem.

Apply the restriction clause of locallyConstantLineTwist_identities to the degree function composed with p on the inverse image of its degree-m open stratum. Membership is exactly the required equality of degrees.

For two decompositions tensor their isomorphisms and use tensorμ to exchange the middle two factors. Combine the two twist factors by the addition clause of the twist identities, using pointwise addition of locally constant functions. Combine the two pulled-back coefficient factors by the inverse of module_pullback_tensor. Tensor products of invertible coefficient modules are invertible.

On a pullback square first pull back the decomposition isomorphism and split its tensor product by module_pullback_tensor. Pullback of the glued twist is given by the last twist identity. The square equality identifies the two composed degree functions pointwise. For the coefficient line, compare successive pullback with pullback along each composite, use the square equality, then compare to the other successive pullback. The explicit tensor pullback is naturally isomorphic to the ordinary module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints, so it preserves invertibility. These isomorphisms prove the displayed base-change decomposition.

proof_origin.place: Remark 4.2.7, printed p.75; reduction into local normal forms (steps 1-4), local-twist descent (steps 5-8) and the generic twist calculus (steps 5 and 9). The main Lean proof combines them and constructs the tensor and base-change isomorphisms.

It is unsplit on base, live and side-live, and the statement is unchanged. Sources read at the cited places: EGA II Remarque 4.2.7 (printed p.75 = PDF p.72), Stacks 0BDA, 0BXJ including its cocycle proof, and 07VK. I checked every step. Step 1: units of k[t,t^-1,z] are c·t^a. Step 2: the triple-overlap exponents agree, the c_{i0} rescaling gives the def-pc-projective-space-twist transitions, n=1 goes through the P^1 classification (def-sc-p1-standard convention matches), and n=r-1>=1 avoids the false n=0 reading of 0BXJ. Step 3: properness, chart flatness, H^1(P^n,O)=0, the section lift, the Nakayama unit argument, then removing the closed image of the non-generation locus. Step 4: Noetherian approximation, constant P^n_Z limit through lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products, and 0B8W descent with qcqs stages and affine transitions. Steps 5-8: p_*O_P=O_S on all opens, descent of the unit cocycle to N, uniqueness of d and of the class of N. Step 9: base change via representable-unique, plus tensor and dual compatibility. New node lem-sfb-affine-space-invertible-trivial (Pic A^n_k=0, n>=0) is true (0BDA(2)) and not a duplicate (lem-pur-affine-punctured-line-algebra covers only n=1). New node lem-sfb-proper-flat-fibre-section-lifting is true by cohomology and base change (R^1f_*F vanishes near s, so phi^0 is surjective). It is distinct from lem-trf-infinitesimal-vanishing-section-lifting (no flatness, needs every J^n/J^{n+1} vanishing), lem-trf-ample-fibre-section-lifting and lem-sfb-relative-acyclic-direct-image; advisory only. Both new nodes are statement-only, cite their notions, carry three search kinds, and are strictly smaller than the item. Batch-5: lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent is generic Stacks 0B8W limit descent, outside the trace-formula and Poincare-duality assumptions and their proofs, so it is accepted. The declared tool_uses are generic black-box interfaces and accepted. No SGA source is used.
